hero.title: About DogBreedID
hero.subtitle: A Computer Science graduation thesis project exploring deep learning, transfer learning, and model interpretability for fine-grained dog breed classification.

challenge.title: The Challenge
challenge.desc: Fine-grained visual categorization is inherently challenging due to subtle inter-class differences between closely related breeds (such as Golden Retriever vs. Labrador Retriever) paired with large intra-class variation in lighting, pose, age, and coat pattern.

approach.title: Our Approach
approach.desc: We leverage transfer learning on deep Convolutional Neural Networks (ResNet50, EfficientNet-B0, MobileNetV3), fine-tuned on the Stanford Dogs Dataset, paired with Grad-CAM activation maps and ONNX Runtime execution for web deployment.

goals.title: Core Project Objectives
goals.g1Desc: Evaluate trade-offs between classification accuracy, parameter count, and inference latency.
goals.g2Desc: Optimize neural network execution speed for real-time web endpoint serving.
goals.g3Desc: Provide visual attention heatmaps to explain prediction regions and increase model transparency.
goals.g4Desc: Build a modern, interactive web user interface designed for thesis defense and live demonstration.

stack.title: Planned End-to-End Technology Stack
stack.frontendDesc: Single-page web client built with ReactJS, React Router, Lucide icons, and Framer Motion.
stack.backendDesc: Asynchronous Python API server handling file uploads and ONNX Runtime sessions.
stack.aiDesc: Fine-tuned transfer learning weights exported for ONNX inference acceleration.
stack.databaseDesc: Relational database storing user sessions, metadata logs, and analysis history.
